description: This topic covers India's defense capabilities, missile systems, and the pivotal contributions of the Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO). It is a highly crucial subject for defense and civil services competitive exams.

sections.title: DRDO and Major Programs
sections.description: An overview of India's premier defense research organization and its foundational historical programs.

historical_events.significance: Formed by the merger of the Technical Development Establishment of the Indian Army and the Defense Science Organization.
Launched under the leadership of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam to develop five indigenous missiles (Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Nag, Akash - PATNA).

important_facts.fact: The official motto of DRDO is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (Strength's Origin is in Science).
DRDO is headquartered at DRDO Bhavan, New Delhi, and operates under the Ministry of Defense, Government of India.

sections.title: Missile Systems of India
sections.description: Classification and mapping of various strategic and tactical missiles utilized by the Indian Armed Forces.

key_concepts.explanation: A missile that follows a parabolic, unpowered trajectory under the influence of gravity after its initial launch phase. It is highly suitable for delivering nuclear warheads over long or intercontinental ranges.
A guided missile that flies continuously at a relatively constant, low altitude within the atmosphere, actively tracking and destroying specific targets with high precision.

key_associations.extra_info: It is India's first indigenously built Short-Range Ballistic Missile (SRBM).
A family of medium to Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles (ICBM). Agni-V has a range of over 5000 km.
A medium-range mobile defense system capable of targeting multiple aerial threats simultaneously.
A 3rd generation 'Fire and Forget' missile. Its helicopter-launched variant is known as 'Helina'.

sections.title: Defense Equipments and Air Systems
sections.description: Major combat aircraft, multi-barrel rocket launchers, and radar systems developed by Indian defense agencies.

key_concepts.explanation: An indigenously designed, single-engine, fourth-generation Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) developed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and HAL.
An indigenous Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher (MBRL) system developed by DRDO that can fire a salvo of 72 rockets in just 44 seconds.
An indigenous Airborne Early Warning and Control System (AEW&CS) developed by DRDO to act as an 'eye in the sky' for the Indian Air Force.

key_associations.extra_info: A Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) drone designed primarily for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions.
A highly advanced Passive Electronically Scanned Array (PESA) radar that functions as the fire control radar for the Akash Missile System.

sections.title: Naval Defense Systems
sections.description: India's maritime security assets, including advanced submarines, aircraft carriers, and torpedoes.

key_associations.extra_info: India's first indigenously designed and built nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN).
India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited, making India part of an elite group of nations capable of building such carriers.
An indigenously developed, ship-launched, electrically propelled anti-submarine torpedo.
A program to build six Scorpene-class diesel-electric attack submarines for the Indian Navy in collaboration with the Naval Group of France.

sections.title: Important Defense Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts, superlatives, and key personalities associated with Indian defense technology.

important_facts.fact: BrahMos is the world's fastest supersonic cruise missile, developed as a joint venture between India (named after the Brahmaputra river) and Russia (named after the Moskva river).
Under 'Mission Shakti' in March 2019, India successfully tested an Anti-Satellite (ASAT) weapon, destroying a live satellite and becoming the fourth country globally to demonstrate this capability.
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is universally revered as the 'Missile Man of India' for his instrumental role in directing the IGMDP.
Dr. Tessy Thomas is widely known as the 'Missile Woman of India' for being the first woman scientist to head an Indian missile project (Agni-IV).
